summary: PAPER-SCHOLZE-26 extracts Scholze, Berkovich motives (J. Amer. Math. Soc. 39 (2026) 697–764; arXiv 2412.03382v3, hash reproduced). It has 55 items (5 planned, 50 missing), 6 routes and 3 misprints. The item statements are faithful to v3, the one library claim holds, and E1–E3 are right. There are 10 findings: 1 high, 6 medium, 3 low. (1, high) Route 1's 42-item Part II 'coalesces with' BKV's MotivesRigidAnalyticPartII and tells the designer to keep its brief. BKV's review rejected that route five hours after this review accepted it. So the pending DESIGN-MotivesAndAlgebraicCyclesPartII carries this route alone, told to keep a brief it never receives and to reuse RigDA layers that nothing plans. (2) AnalyticStacks AS.0/AS.1, proposed a week earlier, plans the Scholze/Heyer–Mann six-functor extension theorems and sheaves on compact Hausdorff spaces, which the extraction calls uncovered prerequisites. (3) Item 49, étale motives with ℤ-coefficients, is marked planned at MC.4/M.5a, which plan only Nisnevich DM with transfers; nothing plans the comparison target of Proposition 1.13. (4) Route 4 gives cdh and pro-cdh descent, 𝔸¹-invariance over valuation rings and Gabber–Suslin rigidity to S.3/S.5, which do not plan them; LMMT already routes cdh descent for KH elsewhere. (5) Route 6 sends dualizable, compactly assembled and rigid categories to E5:presentability, which is scoped to compact generation. (6) de Jong's alterations (planned at L5), van der Put's compactification and Postnikov completeness have no items. (7) Item 22 states Symⁿ(Ḡ_m) ≅ 𝔸^{n−1} × Ḡ_m, which is false; the paper's isomorphism is for G_m. Low: (8) the missed misprint max→min in Proposition 5.19's Newton-polygon bound, with a counterexample; (9) the missed misprints in Lemma 6.5's proof (r_1 for r_2, a_i for a_j, r_1^n for r_1^{k_i}); (10) missing pointers to Mathlib's SeminormedCommRing, MulRingSeminorm, smoothingFun, CondensedSet and continuousCohomology.

Disclosure. This session reviewed PAPER-SCHOLZE-17 (PR #4688) and red-teamed Česnavičius 21, Nikolaus–Scholze 18 and Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme 24 (PRs #4713, #4708, #4730). Finding /4 cites the accepted PAPER-LAND-MATHEW-MEIER-ETAL-24 extraction and review files (item /93's note and route 1), not any finding of the earlier red team; that red team raised nothing about cdh descent. Finding /5 mentions Nikolaus–Scholze Theorem I.3.6 only as a statement this paper cites. No finding relies on the PAPER-SCHOLZE-17 review.

Versions. I downloaded arXiv 2412.03382v3 on 30 September 2026. Its SHA-256 440b4a82…d484 reproduces the recorded hash. arXiv lists v1 (4 Dec 2024), v2 (19 Nov 2025) and v3 (22 Jan 2026), so v3 is the latest. Crossref for doi 10.1090/jams/1068 shows publication on 11 December 2025, no update-to or relation, and no work with filter updates:10.1090/jams/1068. The JAMS article page returned HTTP 403, so the version of record was not compared, and findings /8 and /9 are scoped to v3.

The whole paper read through pdftotext (all 65 pages, §§1–12 and the references). Pages 34, 35 and 38 were rendered as images to confirm the bars in Proposition 5.17, the max in Proposition 5.19 and the slips in Lemma 6.5.

All 55 items against their locators and statements. Every numbered environment the text parser found (150) is cited by some item except Remark 1.4, which agrees with the review's count. Statements checked line by line include Definitions 2.1, 2.13, 3.1, 3.10, 4.3, 4.10, 5.1, 5.2, 5.15, 5.18, 6.2, 9.1, 10.7 and 11.3; Theorems 2.12, 2.14, 2.18, 3.13, 3.14, 4.1, 4.14, 4.20, 5.14, 5.16, 6.1, 6.3, 6.7, 7.1, 8.9, 8.11, 8.13, 9.2, 11.1 and 11.9; Propositions 1.5, 3.2, 4.25, 5.6, 5.8, 5.9, 5.10, 5.17, 5.19, 8.4, 8.5, 9.3, 9.7, 10.1, 10.3, 11.4, 11.6–11.8 and 12.1–12.4; Lemmas 4.4–4.9, 5.3, 6.4, 6.5, 7.3 and 10.4; Corollaries 6.6, 6.9, 8.2, 8.6, 8.10, 10.2, 10.6 and 11.10. Apart from item 22 (finding /7), the statements are faithful, including the conventions of item 1 (|−1| ≤ 1, R = 0 allowed).

Arguments re-derived: Proposition 2.6 (|n| ≤ 1 + log₂ n, then power-multiplicativity); the pushout and discrete cases of Proposition 3.2; Lemma 6.4's divisor bookkeeping ([x] − [x′] ∼ −pD gives [x] + pΣ[x_i] ∼ [x′] + pΣ[x′_i]); the Y_1/Y_2 count N − (N − 1) = 1 in Theorem 7.1; Lemma 7.3's sign; Lemma 6.5's Hom description Q ⊕ (C^×/(1+C_{<1}))^d ⊗ Q ⊕ Q^{de}; Proposition 5.19's Newton-polygon criterion (finding /8).

The three source issues. E1 ('pm1', p. 14, the ring written with ± one clause later), E2 (P¹_A for P¹_C on pp. 36–37, three places in the text) and E3 (Example 3.6 needs A analytic: for ℤ with the trivial norm the residue fields are discrete, and Definition 3.10(i) and Proposition 3.11 require non-discrete fields) are all confirmed. Each appears once in research/errata/REGISTER.md and once in data/source-issues.json. No errata file duplicates them. sourceVersions is absent from the extraction, but none of E1–E3 affects a stated result, so scripts/check_errata.py does not require it, and readSections records v3 with its hash.

Candidate source issues considered and not raised: 'Up the action of SL_2' (p. 43) and 'In all cases it easy to check' (p. 18) are grammar only; '|n|_ℤ = ±n' (p. 8) is a sign-normalised absolute value; Theorem 6.3's 'modulo n for some n ≥ 1' without |n| ≥ 1 is consistent, because Lemma 6.4 holds for every prime p ([p] is surjective on a semiabelian variety) and Theorem 6.7 makes p invertible where |p| < 1.

Every cited layer, read at its stage text in research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps: TB.0 and TB.1; GeneralAlgebraicKTheory K.5; SchemeKTheoryOperations S.3, S.5 and S.6; RefinedTraceMethods RT.5; EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5 (abstract, presentability, animation); MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.4; MotivicEtaleKTheory M.5 and M.5a; KTheoryFiniteLocalFields L.1; AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L5; plus the stage texts of the new roadmaps AnalyticStacks AS.0–AS.4 and SolidAnalyticRings SA.0–SA.4.

Packets and their dates: TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic (partial; TB.0 nodes on MulRingSeminorm, BP pending); GeneralAlgebraicKTheory--K.1 (K.5 source_decomposed, done 28 September; node K.5/excision-and-its-failure covers homologically unital excision, so route 3 lands correctly and item 36 is now plannable there); GeneralAlgebraicKTheory--K.6; SchemeKTheoryOperations (partial, BP pending); EnhancedDerivedSheaves--E5 (partial); MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles (accepted 25 September; all 31 MC.4 nodes). No source route lands in a blueprint that was finished before 23 September.

Routes and owners. I read PAPER-BINDA-KATO-VEZZANI-25's result and review (route 13 rejected, verdict revise), make_queue.py's accepted_routes and paper_designs, queue.json, issues.json and the body of issue #3463 (DESIGN-MotivesAndAlgebraicCyclesPartII); PAPER-SCHOLZE-12's routes with RT-PAPER-SCHOLZE-12/2 and its review; PAPER-LAND-MATHEW-MEIER-ETAL-24 items /34, /90, /92 and /93 and its routes; PAPER-BHATT-MATHEW-21 (arc-topology items, DESIGN-ArcTopologyAndDescent pending); and papers.json for the prerequisites (Bhatt–Mathew was already extracted; Scholze 2017 joined on 29 September, after this extraction). Searching all paper extractions turned up no other owner for Efimov's K-theory, dualizable categories, Tor-unital excision, arc-sheaves on Banach rings or étale motives. There are no cycles: nothing imports the Part II.

Libraries at the pins (Mathlib 082e2d3, Tau Ceti f790474). The one library claim is right: NormedAlgebra.Real.nonempty_algEquiv_or (GelfandMazur.lean:406, for a NormedField that is a NormedAlgebra over ℝ) and NormedAlgebra.Complex.nonempty_algEquiv (:249), and Mathlib has no Ostrowski step from |2| > 1 to an ℝ-algebra structure (Ostrowski.lean covers ℚ only; Ultra.lean:139 isUltrametricDist_iff_forall_norm_natCast_le_one is for division rings, not Proposition 2.6). declarations.tsv has nothing for Berkovich spectra, Banach rings in Scholze's sense, arc-topologies, motives, algebraic K-theory, six-functor formalisms or dualizable categories in either library; the Tau Ceti hits for 'Tate', 'arc' and 'Hodge' are unrelated. Partial Mathlib support is recorded as finding /10.

The review's changes: it corrected, rejected and deleted nothing, so it introduced no errors. Its claims that the Part II title reproduces the parent's title and that there are 50 missing items, each routed once, check out. Its argument for coalescing (same id, title, parent and area as BKV's route) is what finding /1 shows to have no effect.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-SCHOLZE-26.result.json: route 1 (part-ii, roadmap MotivesRigidAnalyticPartII) brief, title and reason; notes of items 17, 27, 44, 50 and 52; PAPER-SCHOLZE-26.md 'What the atlas already has' and 'Routes' 1
findings.claim: Route 1 rests on a coalescence that does not happen. Its brief begins 'This route coalesces with MotivesRigidAnalyticPartII, proposed by PAPER-BINDA-KATO-VEZZANI-25; keep its id, title, parent, area and brief', adds Berkovich motives 'as a Berkovich branch reusing the Part II's formal layers', says the paper reproves 'several of its planned endpoints' (RigDA tilting, good-reduction generation, nearby cycles), and asks for a separate RigDA comparison target. Its reason says 'The pending Part II owns rigid-analytic motives'. Five item notes say the coalesced Part II 'already carries' or 'carries' RigDA versions of items 17, 27, 44, 50 and 52. But the review of PAPER-BINDA-KATO-VEZZANI-25 (committed 2026-09-23 23:58 +0100, about five hours after this extraction's review at 18:35 +0100) rejected exactly that route (its route 13) and gave the paper verdict 'revise'. make_queue.py's accepted_routes returns no routes for a paper whose review verdict is not 'accept', so none of BKV's routes is queued. The design job DESIGN-MotivesAndAlgebraicCyclesPartII (issue #3463) therefore carries this route alone. Its prompt says 'The paper extractions propose 1 continuation in this direction' and points only to PAPER-SCHOLZE-26.result.json. The designer is told to 'keep' a rejected brief it is never given, and to reuse RigDA layers that nothing plans. The title, '... Part II: rigid analytic and logarithmic motives', names logarithmic motives, which this paper never uses. As written, the brief either makes the design rebuild BKV's rejected RigDA/log-motive programme (whose review left gaps G3–G5, G7, G8 and G11 open) or leaves the 'reproved endpoints' and the RigDA comparison without an owner.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-SCHOLZE-26.result.json: item 42 (six-functor formalism on small arc-stacks) statement and note; prerequisites entries 1 (Scholze, Six-Functor Formalisms; Heyer–Mann) and 12 (Bhatt–Mathew); route 1 brief ('Prerequisites: Scholze's Six-Functor Formalisms and Heyer–Mann …'); item 14 (Theorem 4.14)
findings.claim: The atlas already plans the abstract six-functor machinery that item 42 uses, but the extraction treats it as uncovered. Item 42 builds D_mot on small arc-stacks 'from the extension theorems [Sch25b, Thm 5.19], [HM24, Thm 3.4.11]'. Its note says 'the atlas has six operations only for diamonds (DiamondSixOperations) and étale sheaves'. Prerequisite 1 lists both works as papers the atlas does not yet cover, and the brief imports them only as 'Prerequisites'. Yet the proposed roadmap AnalyticStacks (research/blueprint/roadmaps/AnalyticStacks.json, in the repository since 2026-09-16, a week before the extraction) plans in AS.0 exactly these theorems: Mann's construction principle, extension to stacks (Scholze Theorem 5.19 = Heyer–Mann Theorem 3.4.11), and cohomologically smooth, proper and étale maps. Its AS.1 plans the six-functor formalism X ↦ Shv(X, D(ℤ)) on locally compact Hausdorff spaces (Lecture VII). The paper uses that formalism over ℂ: Theorem 4.14 identifies finitary sheaves with the left-complete D(M(A), ℤ), and the proof of Theorem 9.2 uses 'the usual projection formula in topology'. Other extractions already cite AnalyticStacks or SolidAnalyticRings stages, among them the accepted PAPER-BOXER-PILLONI-26, PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23, PAPER-HACON-WITASZEK-23 and PAPER-ZAVYALOV-25. AnalyticStacks' boundaries say its non-goals include 'the motivic Lectures XI–XII', so the Berkovich formalism itself stays in route 1, but its abstract inputs are owned. Separately, prerequisite 12 lists Bhatt–Mathew, which its own 'why' says is 'extracted as PAPER-BHATT-MATHEW-21'. Prerequisites are 'the papers this one builds on that the atlas does not yet cover' (PROTOCOL §16).

Cohomologically smooth maps (Scholze Definition 5.1) … cohomologically étale (Definition 6.12)'. AS.1: 'Locally compact Hausdorff spaces (Lecture VII) … The six-functor formalism X ↦ Shv(X, D(ℤ)) with E all maps (Theorem 7.4)'. Readme boundaries: 'DiamondSixOperations … Their abstract statements are instances of AS.0 once they import it'; non-goals: 'the motivic Lectures XI–XII'. Git: AnalyticStacks.json first committed c69bcc92, 2026-09-16. Scholze 2026 (arXiv v3) p. 52: 'By general extension procedures, cf. [Sch25b, Theorem 5.19] and [HM24, Theorem 3.4.11], we get a 6-functor formalism X ↦ Dmot(X) on all small arc-stacks'; p. 50: 'The case C = ℂ is trivial, using Theorem 4.14 and the usual projection formula in topology'. The accepted extractions PAPER-BOXER-PILLONI-26, PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23, PAPER-HACON-WITASZEK-23 and PAPER-ZAVYALOV-25 cite AnalyticStacks or SolidAnalyticRings stage ids.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-SCHOLZE-26.result.json: item 49 (Voevodsky's category of étale motives over a field), status 'planned' at MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles:MC.4 and MotivicEtaleKTheory:M.5a; item 48 and route 1 brief ('MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.4 and MotivicEtaleKTheory M.5a (Voevodsky's motives, …)')
findings.claim: Item 49 is marked planned, but neither layer plans the category the paper compares with. Item 49 and Remark 11.2 describe étale motives with ℤ-coefficients: the free presentable stable ∞-category generated by smooth k-schemes, subject to étale descent, 𝔸¹-invariance and G_m-stability. Item 48 (Theorem 11.1 = Proposition 1.13) proves D_mot(k) equivalent to it. MC.4 plans Voevodsky's Nisnevich DM, and its accepted packet builds it as the triangulated DM^eff,-_Nis(k,R) of Mazza–Voevodsky–Weibel, with transfers, geometric motives and resolution-of-singularities hypotheses. M.5a plans 'Nisnevich sheaves with transfers'. Nothing plans étale descent, the étale-local presentable ∞-category, or the comparison with transfers. Searching the atlas extracts, the new roadmaps, the packets and the campaign documents for 'étale motives', 'DA^ét' or 'DM_ét' returns nothing. The only other hit is BKV's item /060, 'Algebraic rational étale motives', marked planned at MC.4 in an extraction whose review verdict is 'revise'. So Proposition 1.13 would be proved against an owner that does not exist.

findings.fix: Set item 49 to 'missing', with no planned stage. Keep MC.4 in its note as the Nisnevich, triangulated, with-transfers analogue. Route it with route 1, adding to the brief a layer for étale motives DM_ét(k, ℤ) (étale descent, 𝔸¹-invariance, G_m-stability, as in Remark 11.2) that imports MC.4 and M.5a for transfers and cancellation. findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-SCHOLZE-26.result.json: item 37 (K-theory inputs: Thomason–Trobaugh, cdh and pro-cdh descent, 𝔸¹-invariance over valuation rings, Gabber–Suslin rigidity) and route 4 (source SchemeKTheoryOperations S.3, S.5)
findings.claim: Route 4 sends five separate theorems to two layers that do not plan most of them, and one of them already has a different owner. Item 37 bundles: (a) Thomason–Trobaugh Prop. 3.19 (K-theory with supports unchanged under T-adic completion); (b) Cisinski's cdh descent for KH; (c) pro-cdh descent (Morrow Thm 3.7; Kerz–Strunk–Tamme Thm A); (d) 𝔸¹-invariance of K-theory over valuation rings, which are non-noetherian here (O_C); and (e) Gabber–Suslin rigidity under change of algebraically closed field (used for Theorem 8.9 with torsion coefficients). S.3 can take (a), since it plans excision for supports. But S.5 plans homotopy invariance only 'for regular noetherian schemes in scope', and defines KH 'only if it is used'. Neither stage mentions cdh or pro-cdh descent, valuation rings or rigidity, and the SchemeKTheoryOperations packet's only S.5 node is the Bass fundamental theorem. PAPER-LAND-MATHEW-MEIER-ETAL-24, accepted about an hour before this extraction's review, already says that S.5 does not plan cdh descent for KH. It routes that theorem, inside its item /90, to a GeneralAlgebraicKTheory Part II, so (b) now has two owners. Item 37 also breaks the rule 'Split multi-part results' (PROTOCOL §16).

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-SCHOLZE-26.result.json: item 47 (dualizable, compactly assembled and rigid categories) and route 6 (source EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:presentability)
findings.claim: Route 6 sends the non-compactly-generated theory the paper depends on to a layer whose text is scoped to compact generation. Item 47 bundles eight results: Ramzi's 'compactly assembled ⟺ dualizable' (Thm 2.39) and trace-class generation (Ramzi 2024b, Cor. 4.57), Gaitsgory–Rozenblyum rigidity, rigidity of relative tensor products, Robalo's inversion of a symmetric object, Nikolaus–Scholze's symmetric monoidal Verdier quotients, Barr–Beck–Lurie and Mathew's descendable algebras. The paper uses them because D_mot is usually not compactly generated (p. 63: 'compact generation is not true anymore, but the categories are usually still compactly assembled'). E5:presentability plans Ind-completion, compact objects and extensions 'under the appropriate compact-generation hypotheses', and its packet has no node on dualizable or compactly assembled categories. The route's reason ('compactly assembled and dualizable presentable categories, rigidity, Robalo's inversion … are the presentable-category statements the paper uses') attributes to E5 a scope its text does not have. Meanwhile item 38 routes Efimov's K-theory of dualizable categories to RefinedTraceMethods RT.5, which plans 'compact/dualizable objects, the relevant continuous extensions'. So the notion of dualizable category is sent to two layers, one of which excludes it.
findings.evidence: EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:presentability stage text: 'construct Ind-completion, compact-object comparison and extension of exact functors to colimit-preserving functors. Prove the tensor/Ind and module/base-change compatibilities under the appropriate compact-generation hypotheses.' findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-SCHOLZE-26.result.json: items 44 (Proposition 10.1), 48 (Theorem 11.1), 26 (Lemma 6.4), 15 (Theorem 4.20); no item or prerequisite for the cited inputs
findings.claim: Several key theorems the proofs invoke have no item, and so no status and no route. The main one is de Jong's alteration theorem. Proposition 10.1 uses it to show that D_mot(C) is generated by motives with good reduction, and through it Theorem 1.12 (second sentence) and the generation statement of Theorem 11.1 depend on it. Item 44 mentions it only in a note ('with de Jong's alterations'). The atlas plans it: AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L5 plans de Jong's Theorems 4.1 and 6.5. A second is the divisibility argument of Lemma 6.4: van der Put's Cor. 1.3, that a curve minus finitely many discs has a smooth projective compactification, and the moduli of degree-0 line bundles with trivialisations at boundary points is a semiabelian variety, on which multiplication by p is surjective. A third is that hypercomplete arc-sheaves are Postnikov complete because the arc-topos is replete (Mondal–Reinecke). Theorem 4.20 uses this to pass from D⁺ to D. These last two appear only inside other items' statements or notes, with neither a status nor an entry in prerequisites.
findings.evidence: Scholze 2026 (arXiv v3) proof of Proposition 10.1, p. 53: 'Using alterations, we can arrange that Spec(R_i) ⊂ X_i has a smooth projective compactification X_i whose boundary is a normal crossing divisor.' Proof of Lemma 6.4, p. 37: 'we can find a smooth projective compactification X of U such that Z = X \ U is a finite union of closed discs, see [vdP80, Corollary 1.3] … This is a semiabelian variety, and in particular multiplication by p is surjective.' Proof of Theorem 4.20, p. 24: 'We use that all hypercomplete arc-sheaves are Postnikov complete, as the arc-topos is replete, see [MR25].' AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L5 stage text: 'Prove the forms of de Jong, Smoothness, semi-stability and alterations, Theorems 4.1 and 6.5 used by the comparison'. PAPER-SCHOLZE-26.result.json prerequisites: none of de Jong, van der Put or Mondal–Reinecke.

findings.claim: Item 22 misstates the key step of Proposition 5.17. It says 'ℤ_mot[G_m]/ℤ_mot[∗] ≅ Ḡ_m via characteristic polynomials Symⁿ(Ḡ_m) ≅ 𝔸^{n−1} × Ḡ_m'. The paper's isomorphism is Symⁿ(G_m) ≅ 𝔸^{n−1} × G_m, for the unreduced multiplicative group: a point of Symⁿ(G_m) is a monic degree-n polynomial with unit constant term. The reduced sheaves appear only in the bottom row, Symⁿ(Ḡ_m) → Ḡ_m, which becomes an isomorphism only after passing to ball-invariant sheaves. The vertical maps are 𝔹-homotopy equivalences. With bars the stated isomorphism is false. The coefficients a_1, …, a_{n−1} of ∏(X − x_i) are not defined when the x_i are known only modulo 1-units: changing x_1 by a factor u ∈ 1 + O_{<1} changes a_{n−1} = −Σx_i by (u − 1)x_1 ≠ 0. And Ḡ_m(C) = C^×/(1 + C_{<1}) is invariant under change of algebraically closed field up to value group and residue field, while 𝔸^{n−1}(C) = C^{n−1} is not. A formaliser following item 22 would try to build a map that does not exist.
findings.evidence: Scholze 2026 (arXiv v3) proof of Proposition 5.17, p. 34 (checked on the rendered page image): 'In our case we have, for n ≥ 1, a commutative diagram Symⁿ(G_m) → 𝔸^{n−1} × G_m over Symⁿ(Ḡ_m) → Ḡ_m, where the upper map is given by the characteristic polynomial and is an isomorphism of arc-sheaves. The left vertical and right vertical maps are (colimits of) 𝔹-homotopy equivalences … thus, the lower map is an isomorphism when mapping to ball-invariant sheaves'. The upper row has no bars; the lower row has them.
findings.fix: Replace the clause with: 'via the characteristic-polynomial isomorphism Symⁿ(G_m) ≅ 𝔸^{n−1} × G_m of arc-sheaves; the maps Symⁿ(G_m) → Symⁿ(Ḡ_m) (writing Ḡ_m = |G_m × (1 + O_{<1})^•|) and 𝔸^{n−1} × G_m → Ḡ_m are colimits of 𝔹-homotopy equivalences, so Symⁿ(Ḡ_m) → Ḡ_m becomes an isomorphism after L_B, and ℤ_mot[Ḡ_m]/ℤ_mot[∗] = colim_n Symⁿ(Ḡ_m) (Proposition 5.17)'.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-SCHOLZE-26.result.json: sourceIssues (no entry for the proof of Proposition 5.19, p. 35); item 23
findings.claim: The extraction misses a misprint in the Newton-polygon step of Proposition 5.19. The paper states that X^n + a_{n−1}X^{n−1} + … + a_0, with a_0 ∈ T(r_1^n, r_2^n), has all zeros in T(r_1, r_2) exactly when |a_i| < max(r_2^{n−i}, |a_0| r_1^{−i}) for i = 1, …, n−1. It should be min. Counterexample: C algebraically closed with |C^×| ⊇ 2^ℚ, r_1 = 1/2, r_2 = 4, n = 2, a_0 = 1 ∈ T(1/4, 16) and |a_1| = 2^{3/2} ≈ 2.83. Then |a_1| < max(4, 2) = 4, but the roots have absolute values |a_1| = 2^{3/2} and |a_0|/|a_1| = 2^{−3/2} ≈ 0.354 < 1/2, so one root is outside T(1/2, 4). Proof of the corrected criterion: for a monic polynomial the largest root has absolute value max_{i<n} |a_i|^{1/(n−i)} and the smallest min_{i≥1} (|a_0|/|a_i|)^{1/i}. So all roots lie in (r_1, r_2) if and only if |a_i| < r_2^{n−i} and |a_i| < |a_0| r_1^{−i} for all i. The conclusion is unaffected: the fibre is still an open polydisc, of radii min(r_2^{n−i}, |a_0| r_1^{−i}).
findings.evidence: Scholze 2026 (arXiv v3) p. 35, rendered page image: 'with given a_0 ∈ T(r_1^n, r_2^n) has all zeros in T if and only if all slopes of the Newton polygon defined by a_{n−1}, …, a_1, a_0 lie in the interval (r_1, r_2). This means |a_i| < max(r_2^{n−i}, |a_0| r_1^{−i}) for all i = 1, …, n − 1, which is indeed an open ball.' The same text is in the SHA-256-verified v3 file the extraction used. v3 is the latest arXiv version, Crossref records no update, and the JAMS page could not be opened (HTTP 403).

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-SCHOLZE-26.result.json: sourceIssues (no entry for the surjectivity step in the proof of Lemma 6.5, p. 38); item 26
findings.claim: The extraction misses four slips in one paragraph of the proof of Lemma 6.5. The setting is U = D(0, < r_2) \ ⋃_{i=1}^d D(a_i, ≤ r_1) with r_2 > 1 > r_1, the a_i distinct mod the maximal ideal, t ∈ V = T(s_1, s_2), and a root T of ∏(T − a_i)^{k_i} = t with n = Σk_i. (1) 'if we had |T| ≥ r_1 > 1' should read |T| ≥ r_2 > 1, since r_1 < 1 and the outer boundary of U is |T| = r_2. (2) 'the left-hand side has absolute value r_2^n' should read |T|^n ≥ r_2^n. (3) 'for all other j we have |T − a_i| = |a_i| ≤ 1' should read |T − a_j| = |a_i − a_j| = 1, since |T − a_i| ≤ r_1 < 1 and |a_i − a_j| = 1. (4) 'at most r_1^n, which is < s_1 < |t| once n is sufficiently large' should read at most r_1^{k_i}, once k_i is sufficiently large: the other factors have absolute value 1, so the product is |T − a_i|^{k_i} ≤ r_1^{k_i}, which is at least r_1^n. The argument works as intended, because all k_i are taken large.
findings.evidence: Scholze 2026 (arXiv v3) p. 38, rendered page image: 'U = D(0, < r_2) \ ⋃_{i=1}^d D(a_i, ≤ r_1) for some r_2 > 1 > r_1 and a_i ∈ O_C, pairwise distinct in the residue field k … Now if we had |T| ≥ r_1 > 1, then as all |a_i| ≤ 1, the left-hand side has absolute value r_2^n, which is > s_2 > |t| once n is sufficiently large. On the other hand, if for some i we have |T − a_i| ≤ r_1, then for all other j we have |T − a_i| = |a_i| ≤ 1, and the absolute value of the left-hand side is at most r_1^n, which is < s_1 < |t| once n is sufficiently large.'

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-SCHOLZE-26.result.json: items 1, 5, 9 and 14 (library field empty, no library note); item 4 note
findings.claim: Four missing items do not cite pinned Mathlib declarations that supply part of them. PROTOCOL §16 and the expansion protocol ('Check the local mathematical library before claiming a construction is new') ask for this. (i) Item 1: Scholze's seminormed rings are Mathlib's SeminormedCommRing with ‖1‖ ≤ 1. |−1| ≤ 1 gives |−x| = |x|, so d(x,y) = |x − y| is the pseudometric, and norm_mul_le is submultiplicativity. His Banach rings are NormedCommRing plus CompleteSpace, and the unbundled forms are RingSeminorm and RingNorm. (ii) Item 4 (and the TB.0 packet, which already builds on it): points of M(R) are MulRingSeminorm R bounded by |·|. (iii) Item 5: Prop. 2.21's x ↦ lim |xⁿ|^{1/n} is Mathlib's smoothingFun, which is power-multiplicative for any RingSeminorm with μ 1 ≤ 1, Scholze's standing condition, without a nonarchimedean hypothesis. (iv) Item 9: Prop. 3.9's target site, compact Hausdorff spaces with finite jointly surjective covers, is the coherent topology on CompHaus that defines Mathlib's Condensed/CondensedSet; CompHaus.effectiveEpiFamily_tfae identifies its covering families with finite jointly surjective ones. (v) Item 14: Prop. 4.15's continuous group cohomology is Mathlib's continuousCohomology of topological representations. None of these makes the items 'library'. They are the baseline the planned nodes must reuse.
